# Source-text-only tests, grandfathered.
#
# Every entry below is a test whose assertions only check that a source file
# contains a string. Such a test passes against a broken implementation, so it
# is not regression coverage - it is a spelling check on the code.
#
# THIS FILE MAY ONLY SHRINK.
#   * scripts/check-source-grep-tests.py rejects a pull request that adds an
#     entry, and rejects an entry whose test no longer asserts on source text at
#     all (fix the test, then delete its line).
#   * An entry may NOT be deleted just because its test acquired a behavioural
#     assertion. The line goes when the last source grep goes, not before -
#     otherwise "add one assertion, delete one line" drains the ledger without
#     fixing anything.
#   * To remove an entry, rewrite the test so it asserts on behaviour: drive the
#     function or state machine and check the value or event it produces. Prove
#     it by reverting the production change and watching the test fail.
#   * Never add an entry to make a new test pass. Write a behavioural test.
#   * No key may be ADDED, for any reason - not even to re-key an entry whose
#     test moved to another file. A move and a replacement are indistinguishable
#     from a test name, so moving a grandfathered test means fixing it first.
#
# WHAT THE DETECTOR DOES NOT SEE. Being absent from this file is not a
# certificate that a test asserts on behaviour. Known gaps, worst first:
#   * ONE ASSERTION THAT CALLS ANYTHING clears a whole test. "Behavioural
#     evidence" is an assertion that mentions a binding produced by a call, or
#     hands source text to production code, or contains a call whose head
#     identifier is not a string method (see TEXT_METHODS). Nothing checks that
#     the call has anything to do with the subject, so
#     `assert_eq!(Some(1).unwrap(), 1);` added beside three `source.contains`
#     greps takes the test from rejected to accepted. Measured, on this tree.
#     Narrowing it to "the call must involve the fixture or a binding" was
#     tried and rejected: it misclassifies two existing behavioural tests that
#     call production functions with literal arguments
#     (`subtitle_style_label`, `format_scale`, `player_command_registry`).
#   * a grep hidden inside a helper with a neutral name, e.g.
#     `assert!(has_expected_implementation(source))`. Telling a grep helper from
#     a parser needs flow analysis. A helper whose name contains "assert" is
#     treated as an assertion helper and does not launder the grep; any other
#     name does. The ledger is keyed on the `include_str!` binding rather than
#     on a surviving visible grep, so using this route no longer also drains an
#     entry out of this file - but it still clears the test.
#   * source text read without `include_str!`, e.g. `fs::read_to_string(
#     "src/foo.rs")`. None exist today.
#   * a helper in ANOTHER module that returns source text. A helper in the same
#     file whose return type is a string is resolved; a cross-module one is not.
#   * a test that asserts on behaviour but on the wrong thing. This check reads
#     shapes, never meaning: it cannot tell a real regression test from one that
#     drives the code and asserts something trivially true.
#   * C#. The pattern exists only in the Rust workspace.
#
# Two of those gaps are one token wide. This check is a floor against writing a
# grep-only test by habit, not a defence against an author who wants one merged.
#
# Format: <path relative to the repository root>::<test function name>

rust/crates/okp-core/tests/isolated_xvfb_session.rs::main_window_fit_session_has_one_multiscreen_manager_and_two_supervisors

# Found by the sharpened classifier, not newly written. Each of these three
# already existed on main and was hidden from the first version of the detector:
#   * player_close_returns_to_gtk_before_mpv_teardown bound its text through a
#     tuple pattern (`let (before_idle, idle_body) = ...`), which the binding
#     tracker did not read;
#   * the other two were cleared by a constant-to-constant assertion
#     (`assert_eq!(SETTINGS_SWITCH_WIDTH, 39)`), which used to count as
#     behaviour.
#   * portability_media_smokes_use_isolated_sessions_and_wait_for_xfwm walked
#     its texts straight out of a `for … in [include_str!(..), …]` array, which
#     bound nothing the tracker could see;
#   * playback_chrome_keeps_the_canonical_redlines was cleared by a `.contains`
#     search on a constant stylesheet - searching a string is not running code.

# Found when this branch was updated from main after #637 and #388 merged. All
# three tests already existed on main, and each pins a property of a packaging
# or build artifact that no Rust unit test in this workspace can drive, so
# there is no cheap behavioural form to rewrite them into:
#   * native_wayland_screenshots_use_libmpv_advanced_control would need a live
#     Wayland display and a real libmpv render context to observe;
#   * fedora_launch_closure_keeps_its_dlopen_requires_and_weak_dependency_exclusions
#     asserts on the Fedora spec, the RPM workflow and the install gate script;
#     its behavioural form is the installed-RPM launch job those files describe;
#   * windows_installed_tree_assertion_keeps_a_size_floor_under_every_required_file
#     asserts on a PowerShell script and the Windows packaging workflow, neither
#     of which runs on Linux.
rust/crates/okp-linux-gtk/src/tests.rs::native_wayland_screenshots_use_libmpv_advanced_control
rust/crates/okp-linux-gtk/src/tests.rs::fedora_launch_closure_keeps_its_dlopen_requires_and_weak_dependency_exclusions
rust/crates/okp-linux-gtk/src/tests.rs::windows_installed_tree_assertion_keeps_a_size_floor_under_every_required_file
